dialogues.speaker: Bazhenov
dialogues.text: When it comes to Snezhnaya's safety and security, even the smallest error is unacceptable...

dialogues.speaker: Bazhenov
dialogues.text: I'm carrying out a security inspection, traveler. Snezhnograd Central Station is the lifeline of the city, and our city is the very heart of Snezhnaya itself.

dialogues.speaker: Bazhenov
dialogues.text: Look at the area I'm responsible for, the exit gates. They're one of the station's most important checkpoints, wouldn't you say?

dialogues.speaker: Bazhenov
dialogues.text: For the safety and future of Snezhnaya, we must identify all possible risks and suspicious persons at the earliest, and report these at once.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But it looks safe enough here...

dialogues.speaker: Bazhenov
dialogues.text: That is what it means to prevent trouble before it happens, traveler.

dialogues.speaker: Bazhenov
dialogues.text: Avalanches can happen to you when you least expect it. One moment, you're on a peaceful snow-covered mountain, and the very next, you're running for your life. The same goes for tsunamis — they can rise all of a sudden out of the calmest waters.

dialogues.speaker: Bazhenov
dialogues.text: The calmer a place appears, the more likely it is that hidden currents are moving beneath the surface, with danger lurking everywhere. That is why we must remain vigilant at all times.

dialogues.speaker: Bazhenov
dialogues.text: Just think about it: what if someone is smuggling crystal ore? What if some spy tries to enter Snezhnograd from here to gather information on Her Majesty's whereabouts?

dialogues.speaker: Bazhenov
dialogues.text: What if someone tries to come into the city to scalp theater tickets and disrupt the market? Or what if foreigners arrive hoping to join the Transport Bureau, only to take all the places meant for Snezhnayans?

dialogues.speaker: Bazhenov
dialogues.text: If we allow them into Snezhnograd through the gates, there's no telling how many crises they might bring upon Snezhnaya...

dialogues.speaker: Bazhenov
dialogues.text: Oh... There are far too many possibilities. I mustn't dwell on them. I must focus on my duties.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is all that part of your job too?

dialogues.speaker: Bazhenov
dialogues.text: Now, now... Even if I'm only required to guide passengers out of the station, I'm still a citizen of Snezhnaya. Isn't protecting our homeland's security part of our duty as well?

dialogues.speaker: Bazhenov
dialogues.text: I'll have to stop here, since I must keep my eyes on the exit gates at all times. Please excuse me.
